title: Taking disjoint unions of semirepresentable hypercovers
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small subcanonical site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with fibre products, and fix $T\in\mathcal C$. Subcanonical means every representable presheaf $h_A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,A)$ is a sheaf. Let $K$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] of $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], with $K_n=\{A_{n,i}\to T\}_{i\in I_n}$. Assume its degree-zero and proper-face matching arrows are componentwise covering families (over each target member the corresponding source arrows form a covering). Assume that $A_n=\coprod_{i\in I_n}A_{n,i}$ exists in $\mathcal C/T$ for every $n$, and that the canonical maps $\coprod_{i\in I_n}h_{A_{n,i}}\to h_{A_n}$ are isomorphisms of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$. Then taking disjoint unions of the component maps defines an augmented simplicial object $A_\bullet\to T$ of $\mathcal C$. Every matching arrow $h_{A_n}\to M_n(h_{A_\bullet}/h_T)$ is an epimorphism. Here $M_0=h_T$, and for $n>0$ the matching object is the finite limit of the compatible proper-face diagram in the category of sheaves of sets over $h_T$, so $M_1=h_{A_0}\times_{h_T}h_{A_0}$.

proof.text: Construct A on each simplicial degree from the given coproduct cofan. For an operator use its component maps followed by the target coproduct inclusions, and descend by the given universal property. Test identity and composition on each summand. The degreewise identifications with the supplied coproducts are identity isomorphisms.

Let R_T be the coproduct of representable sheaves in the slice over h_T. It preserves finite limits by the realization lemma. The assumed colimit property of each Yoneda-image cofan also holds in the slice because the slice forgetful functor reflects colimits. Uniqueness of coproducts gives a degreewise isomorphism K composed with R_T to A composed with sheaf Yoneda. Test naturality on each representable summand.

Formal families over T have finite limits: Over T has a terminal object and pullbacks, and the formal-family construction preserves those existence properties. Choose a proper-face matching arrow kappa in degree n using the matching-object existence statements, with separate terminal and binary-product cases in degrees zero and one. Its componentwise covering property is the supplied hcover, so R_T(kappa) is epi by the covering-realization lemma.

Transport the matching cone through R_T and the simplicial natural isomorphism. In degree zero compare terminal objects; in degree one compare binary-product cones; in higher degrees postcompose the finite boundary cone with the natural isomorphism of diagrams. Limit uniqueness gives a target isomorphism, and testing on every face projection expresses the requested matching map as R_T(kappa) conjugated by source and target isomorphisms. It is epi in the sheaf slice and hence its underlying sheaf map is epi.
